Adjunct Professor, School of Earth and Ocean Sciences, University of Victoria. “Large earthquakes in Canada? [A] M7.8 earthquake rocked # HaidaGwaii . This offshore # earthquake was felt to more than 1,000 km distance, caused strong shaking and some damage in nearby communities, landslides, and a significant tsunami. It was followed by 1,000's of aftershocks. Detailed studies (seismic, GPS, tsunami, thermal and more) of this earthquake sequence have greatly improved our understanding of earthquake and tsunami hazards in this region - which, in turn, allows for improved # preparedness and # resilience …” -- “The boundary between the Pacific and North America plates along Canada’s west coast is one of the most seismically active regions of Canada, and is where Canada’s two largest instrumentally recorded earthquakes have occurred. Although this is a predominantly strike-slip transform fault boundary, there is a component of oblique convergence between the Pacific and North America plates off Haida Gwaii. The 2012 Mw 7.7 Haida Gwaii earthquake was a thrust event that generated a tsunami with significant run up of over 7 m in several inlets on the west coast of Moresby Island (several over 6 m, with a maximum of 13 m).
